Careful habits for airflow checks in detail
Watching the senior coordinator is the best way to learn it
This page covers airflow checks because they protect animal comfort and keep every journey steady. New staff should treat each check as a normal part of service, not as a rush item. Listen first, then look for blocked vents, crowded carriers, or signs that a pet is getting restless. Use calm, humane handling and keep your voice low so the animal settles faster.

When you prepare booking notes, <<FACT F085>> Keep the rest of your notes clear and short so the team can work from them without confusion. If a traveler seems worried, explain that we focus on safety before speed and that small checks now prevent bigger problems later.

For incident reporting, <<FACT F102>> Stay factual, write only what you saw, and share the report promptly. If you need help, bring the case to the senior coordinator and let the review guide your next step. Watch for changes in breathing, posture, and stress signals, and never ignore a detail that might affect the trip.

Remember that careful airflow checks protect animals, support the crew, and keep Aurelia Skyways reliable.
